section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion section presents findings from a single study examining the factorial validity of a Chinese (Cantonese) version of the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) among adults in Hong Kong. The study found a two-dimensional factor structure with a 7-item General Body Appreciation factor that showed significant correlations with BMI and self-esteem, with men showing significantly higher body appreciation than women. The authors acknowledge limitations including reliance on a student sample and discuss implications for cross-cultural measurement of body appreciation, noting that the newer BAS-2 warrants examination in different cultural contexts.

section_summary.extract_value: This discussion section presents findings from a single study examining the factorial validity of the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) among a Hong Kong sample. The study found a two-dimensional factor structure rather than the one-dimensional structure reported in the original BAS development, with a truncated 7-item General Body Appreciation factor showing good psychometric properties. The authors discuss how culture-specific factors and potential differential item functioning may explain why the BAS structure differs across cultural contexts, and they recommend using the truncated measure for Cantonese-speaking samples while cautioning against assuming the BAS is one-dimensional.

section_summary.extract_value: This discussion section presents findings from a single study examining the factorial validity of the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) among a Hong Kong sample. The study found a two-dimensional factor structure with a 7-item General Body Appreciation factor and a Body Image Investment factor, differing from the original BAS structure. The results suggest that body appreciation does not share the same conceptual and factorial structure across cultures, with culture-specific factors and possible differential item functioning contributing to these differences.
